title: DC-area forecast: One more perfect day before warmth and humidity make a comeback
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Sunny skies and comfortably dry air. Highs climb into the mid-70s to around 80 this afternoon.

What’s next? It turns warmer Wednesday and warmer still Thursday, while humidity slowly creeps back in. A cold front approaches late in the week, bringing rain chances that bear watching into the weekend.

Today's daily digit — 10/10: Wall-to-wall sunshine, refreshingly dry air, and highs from the mid-70s to around 80 — about as perfect as a September day gets. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Tuesday): Sunny, with just a few high clouds arriving later in the day. Comfortable highs in the mid-70s to near 80. Winds stay light and variable, becoming southeast by afternoon. Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Tonight: Mainly clear aside from periodic high clouds. Lows range from the 50s to around 60 downtown. A light southeast breeze calms during the evening. Confidence: High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Wednesday): Sunny — perhaps nearly cloudless — and warmer, with highs in the low to mid-80s. Dew points near 60 keep the slowly increasing humidity tolerable. A light breeze from the south may occasionally gust near 15 mph. Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Tomorrow night: Mostly clear and milder, with lows in the 60s for most of us. A light breeze from the south and southwest helps draw in warmer, more humid air overnight. Confidence: Medium-High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

We turn warmer still Thursday, with highs in the mid-80s to around 90 — assuming the sunnier, drier forecast holds. Humidity edges up too, with dew points reaching the mid-60s. Overnight lows settle mostly in the 60s, although downtown could remain in the low 70s. Confidence: Medium

A cold front approaches from the northwest and may stall nearby Friday into the weekend, bringing chances for showers and thunderstorms, especially during the afternoon and evening. Some models suggest the front could move more slowly and produce more rain than currently forecast, which would increase daily rain chances from the roughly 30 percent currently expected.

Otherwise, expect variably cloudy skies with warm, somewhat muggy conditions. Highs are mainly in the 80s, with lows in the 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Low-Medium

DC weather history for September 15

Intense late-summer heat in 1930 pushed temperatures to 97 degrees, part of a prolonged hot and dry stretch during one of the region’s worst droughts on record.
